### Questions about searching Irish planning applications

#### How do I search Irish planning applications on PlanIntel?

Type an address, townland, Eircode, a word from the proposal, or a planning reference such as F13B/0090 into the search box. Results can be filtered by local authority, outcome (granted or refused), application type and decision year, and every result links to its record page and the council source. Search is free and needs no account. The index covers 493,447 applications across 30 local authorities.

#### Which Irish local authorities does PlanIntel cover?

30 of Ireland's 31 planning authorities are indexed from the National Planning Applications dataset published on data.gov.ie. Cork City is the exception: it is not in that national dataset yet. Council documents are read directly from the council portals for Carlow, Cavan, Clare, Dublin City, Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown, Fingal and Wicklow.

#### Where do the refusal reasons come from?

From the council's written decision for that application. The documents are downloaded from the council portal, converted to text, and read by a model that pulls out each refusal reason and the sentence it came from. Each quote is checked word for word against the document text before it is shown. 8,858 applications have been read this way so far.

#### Is PlanIntel free to use?

Search, record pages and county refusal trends are free without an account. A free account can open the refusal reasons and source links on one record, watch one application, and ask the planning chat 5 questions a day. The Home plan is €29 a year for unlimited reason unlocks, watches and nearby alerts. A one-off site risk brief is €39 incl. VAT, and Pro is €19 a month for full archive search depth and CSV export.

#### Can PlanIntel tell me whether my planning application will be granted?

No. PlanIntel shows what nearby applications were decided, why refusals happened, and the documents behind those decisions. It is a research tool built from public records, not planning advice, and it does not predict a decision. Check the current development plan and take qualified advice before applying.

# Page 2: How Irish Planning AI reads council records / PlanIntel

Source URL: https://planintel.ie/about

Skip to content

## How PlanIntel's Irish Planning AI works

I'm Tashfeen. I build AI software for a living, and PlanIntel is a one-person Irish planning AI project: no office, no team, no funding. Just me, the AI agents I put to work, a GPU in my home office, and a question that would not go away: why is it so hard to find out how planning decisions actually get made in Ireland?

### The problem

Every planning decision in Ireland is public. The application, the planner's report, the reasons a council refused or approved it. But the records sit across dozens of council portals, inside scanned PDFs, in formats nobody can search. If you want to know why homes like yours get refused in your area, the honest answer has been: hire someone, or spend weeks reading.

### How it works

The whole thing runs on a Dell workstation in my home office, driven by an NVIDIA Tesla P40, a 24 GB datacenter GPU from 2016, working around the clock. A pipeline collects each county's public planning records from the council portals, OCRs tens of thousands of scanned PDFs, and pulls out the decisions, conditions, and refusal reasons in a structured, searchable form. Every record keeps a link back to the council source, so you can always verify what the model extracted. So far it has indexed 493,447 applications and fully analysed 8,858 of them. Most recently it read Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown: 10,214 of 10,280 application files read so far. The next reading session runs on today's schedule.

### The model that reads the documents

At first, every decision document was read by a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It was accurate, but slow on a GPU from 2016. So I took its verified output and used it to fine-tune my own 4-billion-parameter model, trained specifically to read Irish planning decision documents. The smaller model now does most of the reading, roughly ten times faster, and the few documents too large for it still go through the big one.

### Why trust it

The model does the reading, but it never gets the last word. Every quote it pulls out is checked word-for-word against the scanned document text: if a quote is not verbatim in the source, the record is flagged rather than trusted. Extractions are marked with their quality, low-confidence results are flagged on the page, and the original council documents are always one click away. When a document cannot be read, the record says so instead of guessing.

### A small ask

This is an early product built by one person trying to make something genuinely useful. If something looks wrong, confusing, or missing, tell me and I will fix it, usually within a day. And if PlanIntel saved you time, telling a friend or a planning consultant helps more than you know. Write to me at [email protected] . I read everything. And if you want to keep an eye on a site, create a free account — you can save applications, get told when a decision lands, and ask the planning AI a few questions a day. It costs nothing, and it tells me this was worth building.

Irish self-build planning guide

## Can I build a house on this land?

Possibly—but owning a site does not guarantee planning permission. The useful first question is whether the site, local policy, access, servicing, and nearby decisions support a credible application.

Check my site for €39 incl. VAT Search one-off house decisions

The short answer

### Start with evidence, not a promise.

Irish planning decisions are site-specific. A nearby grant can show what worked; a nearby refusal can reveal the risks to address. Neither replaces the current development plan or professional advice.

Site feasibility

### Five checks before you spend on a house design

Work through these in order. Each can change whether the site is viable or what evidence an application needs.

1

#### Planning policy and zoning

Check the current county or city development plan, settlement boundary, zoning, and any rural housing policy that applies to the site. A site outside a settlement may face different tests from one inside it.

2

#### Rural housing need

Some rural areas apply local-need, economic-need, or housing-need criteria. The wording and evidence vary by planning authority and policy area, so read the current plan rather than relying on a nearby approval alone.

3

#### Access and sightlines

A safe entrance, achievable sightlines, road classification, traffic speed, and roadside boundaries can decide whether a house is feasible. Nearby refusals often reveal the access evidence planners expect.

4

#### Wastewater and services

For an unsewered site, ground conditions, percolation, separation distances, water supply, and the proposed treatment system matter. A site-size figure by itself does not prove that wastewater can be handled safely.

5

#### Site constraints and local precedent

Flood risk, protected habitats, archaeology, landscape sensitivity, ribbon development, and nearby planning decisions can all affect the proposal. Precedent is useful evidence, but it never guarantees the same outcome.

### What nearby Irish planning decisions can tell you

Public decisions help you see local refusal themes, accepted access arrangements, recent outcomes, and the source documents behind them. Start broad, then read the closest relevant grants and refusals.

Search access and sightlines Search wastewater decisions

### What precedent cannot tell you

It cannot confirm zoning, prove compliance with today's policy, test a wastewater design, certify sightlines, or guarantee a decision. Use PlanIntel to find and organise evidence, then verify it against the live council plan and qualified advice. How the Irish Planning AI reads records

### Common Irish self-build planning questions

#### Does owning land mean I can build a house on it?

No. Ownership gives you the right to apply, but planning permission depends on the site, the proposed house, current policy, infrastructure, environmental constraints, and the evidence submitted.

#### Do I need planning permission to build a house in Ireland?

A new house normally requires planning permission. Confirm the correct route and current requirements with the relevant planning authority or a qualified planning professional before committing money.

#### Can I build a house on agricultural land?

Agricultural ownership or use does not create an automatic right to build a home. Rural housing policy, need criteria, access, wastewater, landscape, and environmental constraints may all apply.

#### Can Irish Planning AI tell me whether permission will be granted?

No AI can promise a planning outcome. PlanIntel can speed up evidence gathering by finding nearby decisions, extracted refusal themes, and source documents. A planner or other qualified adviser should assess the proposal and current policy.

## Disclaimer

PlanIntel helps users inspect public planning records and precedent. It is not professional planning advice. Last updated 13 July 2026

### Public-record research tool

The product is derived from public planning records, local authority portals, An Coimisiún Pleanála material, and processed document text. Record pages link to the council or government source where available. Users should verify the source file before relying on a record.

### Not advice

Reports, search results, refusal categories, and chat responses are research aids. They are not legal, planning, architectural, engineering, or professional advice. Planning outcomes depend on site facts, policy, timing, submissions, local authority practice, and appeal decisions. We do not predict or guarantee permission.

### AI-generated content

Some reports, summaries, classifications, and chat responses are generated using artificial intelligence. AI-generated content may be incorrect, incomplete, misleading, or out of date. Always check AI-generated content against the linked council or government source records and obtain appropriate professional advice before making a planning, legal, financial, or property decision.

### Data limits

Public sources can be incomplete, delayed, restructured, or corrected by a local authority after we ingest them. If a record looks wrong, use the contact route and include the local authority and planning reference.

# Page 9: DPIA Summary / PlanIntel

Source URL: https://planintel.ie/dpia

Skip to content

PlanIntel legal

## DPIA Summary

This summary records the privacy reasoning for indexing Irish public planning records and making source-linked records searchable. Last updated 13 July 2026

### Processing purpose

The product indexes planning applications, decisions, local authority references, source URLs, decision dates, public document categories, and planning reasons on record so users can research planning precedent. The product does not market to applicants. The plan explicitly forbids emailing applicants from planning files.

### Lawful basis

For public planning-record indexing, the primary GDPR basis is legitimate interests: making already published planning records searchable with source links, while reducing unnecessary personal-data exposure. For accounts, paid reports, and subscriptions, processing is necessary for contract. For receipts, tax, abuse prevention, and security logs, processing may be necessary for legal obligations or legitimate interests.

### Risks and mitigations

Risks include resurfacing personal data from public files, stale council links, overbroad search snippets, and users mistaking precedent analysis for advice. Mitigations include linking back to source portals, not serving archived documents publicly, limiting displayed snippets, providing a de-listing contact route, using account verification, and publishing a clear disclaimer.

### Review

Privacy and de-listing requests go to [email protected] . The DPIA should be reviewed before the first paid subscription and whenever the product adds new sources, personal-data fields, or outbound outreach.

# Page 10: Granny flat planning permission in Ireland: the 27 July 2026 exemption / PlanIntel

Source URL: https://planintel.ie/granny-flat-planning-permission

Skip to content

Exempted development from 27 July 2026

## Granny flat planning permission in Ireland

Since 27 July 2026 a garden dwelling of up to 45 m² behind your house, or a subdivision of the house into a second unit of at least 32 m², can be exempt from planning permission if you notify the council 14 days ahead. The exemption runs to 31 December 2030. Before you rely on it, see what your council decided on the same kind of proposal.

Search granny flat applications Refused granny flats

The source

### Read the Department's own wording.

The facts on this page come from the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage's circular on the 2026 exempted development regulations and its 27 July 2026 announcement . Conditions such as height, boundary distances and the notification form are set out there, not here.

What changed

### The five facts of the 2026 exemption

1

#### In force since 27 July 2026

The Planning and Development (Exempted Development (Act of 2000)) Regulations 2026 came into effect on 27 July 2026.

2

#### Garden dwelling up to 45 m²

A new exemption (Class 3A) covers a detached auxiliary dwelling to the rear of the principal house, linked to the services of the principal house, of between 32 m² and 45 m² floor area.

3

#### Subdividing the house, 32 m² minimum

A new exemption (Class 1A) allows the principal dwelling to be split into up to one additional self-contained unit within the existing building envelope, with a minimum floor area of 32 m² for each subdivided unit.

4

#### Notify the council 14 days before

Both classes require the planning authority to be notified at least 14 days before the development takes place.

5

#### Runs until 31 December 2030

Both exemptions are time-bound and expire on 31 December 2030.

### What PlanIntel adds

The exemption is new; the council records are not. PlanIntel indexes the planning applications of 30 local authorities, so you can see how granny flats, garden studios and family flats were decided in your area before the change, read the refusal reasons where they are live, and open the council's own documents from each record.

Search garden studios Search family flats Pick your county

### What this page does not do

It does not confirm that your proposal is exempt, and it does not restate the regulations in full. A past grant or refusal nearby is evidence of how the council read the old rules, not a ruling on the new ones. Read the circular, and if anything is unclear ask the planning authority or a qualified adviser. Building a whole house instead? Start here

### Granny flat questions

#### Do I still need planning permission for a granny flat?

Only if the proposal falls outside the exemption. A garden dwelling that is not to the rear of the house, not linked to the house's services, or outside the 32 m² to 45 m² floor area range is not covered by Class 3A, and the full conditions in the Department's circular apply. When in doubt, read the circular and ask the planning authority before building.

#### What was being refused before the exemption?

Searching PlanIntel for granny flat, garden studio or family flat returns the applications councils decided under the old rules, including the refused ones, each linked to the council's own decision. Where refusal reasons are live, the record shows why.

#### Does the exemption apply to a log cabin sold on its own?

PlanIntel does not restate conditions beyond the ones listed above. The Department's circular sets out what the detached dwelling must be and how it must relate to the principal house; read it at gov.ie before relying on the exemption.

#### How do I check what my council decided nearby?

Open your county's page on PlanIntel for its refusal rate and recent decisions, or search your townland or Eircode. A free account can watch one application and is told when its decision lands.
